title: Admission shepherd: priority carving, soft-admit path, and utilization prober
author: Asha Khandelwal
release_notes: Introduce an admission shepherd that performs lightweight per-request priority carving and a soft-admit path to prevent wholesale queueing under bursty load; ships utilization prober metrics for better autoscaler signals.
description:
Context: We see frequent short-lived microbursts that cause sharp tail latency spikes when the autoscaler hasn't reacted. Existing throttling is blunt (global headroom gates) and causes either over-admittance or aggressive shedding. This PR introduces an 'admission shepherd' component that: 1) applies priority carving to classify requests into admission buckets, 2) implements a soft-admit path where lower-priority requests are admitted at reduced concurrency/slots instead of being outright rejected, and 3) probes utilization at short intervals with lightweight synthetic samples to expose transient capacity headroom to the autoscaler.

Motivation: Reduce tail latency impact and improve throughput SLOs for critical tenants during transient surges, while preserving some capacity for lower-priority traffic instead of immediate hard-shedding.

Design summary: The admission shepherd sits in the routing layer (redwood/runtime/router) and consults the tiered-priority policy defined in redwood/allocator/policy. For each incoming request it computes a carve score (based on tenant priority, recent token budget usage, and ephemeral fairness score) and routes the request into one of: full-admit, soft-admit, or defer. Soft-admitted requests are placed on a constrained token bucket (lower concurrency, reduced KV cache reservation) and are tagged for lower billing priority. The utilization prober emits two new telemetry streams: probe_success_rate and probe_latency_p95; probes are tiny synthetic requests that exercise the runtime execution path (no model weights, control-path only) and are scheduled adaptively when queue depth exceeds a threshold.

Backward compatibility and config: All behaviour is feature-flagged by the new config flag runtime.admission_shepherd.enabled=false by default. Policies are configurable via YAML in dedicated/allocator/policy.yaml. Soft-admit is opt-in per-tenant with a default global policy that applies to low-priority tenants only.

Checklist:
- [x] Implementation in router/allocator/telemetry
- [x] Unit tests for carve score logic
- [x] Integration test that simulates microbursts and verifies reduced tail latency for high-priority traffic
- [x] New metrics exposed to console and autoscaler
- [x] Docs for policy configuration
- [x] Feature flag and rollout plan

Commits summary: 1) initial scaffold for admission shepherd and priority carve computation (router + allocator glue); 2) soft-admit token-bucket implementation and KV cache reservation hooks; 3) utilization prober implementation and telemetry wiring; 4) tests and docs; 5) follow-up perf tuning after reviewer feedback.

Files changed (high level):
- redwood/runtime/router/admission_shepherd.go (new)
- redwood/allocator/policy/carve_policy.go (new)
- redwood/allocator/soft_admit_bucket.go (new)
- redwood/telemetry/prober.go (new)
- redwood/console/metrics/registry.go (hooked probe metrics)
- redwood/config/defaults.yaml (default flags)
- redwood/docs/ops/admission_shepherd.md (docs)
- tests/integration/admission_shepherd_burst_test.go (integration test)
- tests/unit/carve_policy_test.go
- Makefile/CODEOWNERS updates

Review notes and reasoning: The carve score intentionally keeps state small (per-tenant rolling windows + exponential decay) to avoid memory blowup in large clusters. Soft-admit avoids reserving full KV cache for low-priority requests to keep hot-cache lanes for full-admit traffic. Probes are non-model requests that exercise the code path to detect transient scheduling/backpressure before token-level metrics reflect the saturation.

Testing & CI: Initial CI run had a flaky integration asserting exact queue depth; fixed by relaxing timing assertions and adding a deterministic probe hook for CI runs. All checks green on rerun: unit tests, go vet, linters, integration smoke, and a small performance benchmark that validates p95 latency improvement for high-priority tenants under simulated bursts.

Operational plan: Rollout as feature-flag off to production, enable for canary fleet (10% traffic) with telemetry dashboards for probe_success_rate and soft_admit_evict_count. If stable after 48h, enable on an additional 50% fleet and monitor cost/reliability impact.

b7d8e5a: soft-admit token bucket + KV cache hooks
review_comments: Evan Murphy: Can you outline memory cost of per-tenant rolling windows? Consider a bounded LRU with eviction precision metric.
Asha: added a bounded LRU with exponential decay and documented worst-case memory in carve_policy.go comments
Priya Sinha: Soft-admit looks good but we need a clear billing signal; add a tag to requests so billing pipeline can filter
Asha: added request tags (soft_admit:true) and a console metric soft_admit_billed_tokens
Luca Romano: Probe rate needs throttling to avoid adding load under saturation; can we gate probes behind a token bucket?
Asha: probes are gated and use an adaptive throttle; added tests to ensure probe rate drops to zero under 90% occupancy
notes_on_ci_failures: First CI run failed 1 integration due to timing assertions; adjusted test to use deterministic probe hook in CI; subsequent CI run passed.
high_level_risks: Potential for billing discrepancies if soft-admit tagging is missed; risk mitigated by end-to-end test and will monitor soft_admit_billed_tokens during rollout.
post_merge_tasks: 1) Add dashboard panels to SLO board for probe metrics; 2) Notify SRE to include admission_shepherd.error_rate in paging thresholds; 3) Coordinate billing team to accept soft-admit tokens tag.
